standard.summary: Core numbers of vertices are a widely studied cohesive subgraph model due to their linear running time. In practice, many data graphs are dynamic and continuously change by inserting or removing edges; updating core numbers under such changes is known as core maintenance. Existing parallel approaches were based on the Traversal algorithm and had limited parallelism, but a new parallel core maintenance algorithm based on the Order algorithm provides parallelism even when all vertices share the same core numbers, achieving significant speedups on a 64-core machine for both edge insertions and removals.

citations.claim: The core numbers of vertices in a graph are one of the most well-studied cohesive subgraph models because of the linear running time.
In practice, many data graphs are dynamic graphs that are continuously changing by inserting or removing edges.
The core numbers are updated in dynamic graphs with edge insertions and deletions, which is called core maintenance.
Our new approach always has parallelism, even for the graphs where all vertices have the same core numbers.

balanced.summary: Core numbers of vertices are a well-studied cohesive subgraph model, largely because core decomposition runs in linear time. Real-world data graphs are often dynamic, with continuous edge insertions and removals, so core maintenance—updating core numbers under these changes—is critical. Sequential core maintenance algorithms include Traversal and Order, with Order giving significant speedups (up to 2,083x). However, dynamic core maintenance is fundamentally hard: under OMv and SETH conjectures, no efficient dynamic algorithm exists for k-core or even (2 - epsilon)-approximations, and bounded algorithms that are fast when few core values change are also ruled out, though a polylogarithmic algorithm exists for the special case of 2-core. Broader experimental evaluations compare core-based and other cohesive subgraph models across synthetic and real-world networks to support model selection in practice. Core models also extend to hypergraphs, where new pruning-based approaches improve efficiency.

citations.claim: Core numbers of vertices in a graph are one of the most well-studied cohesive subgraph models because of the linear running time of core decomposition.
In practice, many data graphs are dynamic and continuously change by inserting or removing edges; updating core numbers under such changes is called core maintenance.
The Order sequential algorithm significantly outperforms the Traversal algorithm for core maintenance, with up to 2,083 times speedups on tested graphs.
The k-core of a graph is its maximal subgraph with minimum degree at least k, and the core value of a vertex u is the largest k for which u is contained in the k-core.

Under OMv and SETH conjectures, there is no efficient dynamic algorithm for k-core or for (2 - epsilon)-approximations of core values, and bounded algorithms that are fast when few core values change also do not exist based on the OMv conjecture.
On the positive side, a polylogarithmic dynamic algorithm exists for 2-core.
Cohesive subgraph models, including core-based ones, are evaluated through extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world networks to provide insights into their efficiency and applicability.
Core models extend to hypergraphs, e.g., the (k,g)-core, and a new (k,g,p)-core with pruning algorithms reduces the execution frequency of costly operations by 51.9% on real-world datasets.

standard.summary: QMC rules are equal weight quadrature rules for approximating integrals over [0,1]^s. A line of research studies the integration error of functions in the unit ball of so-called Korobov spaces, which are Hilbert spaces of periodic functions on [0,1]^s with square integrable partial mixed derivatives of order alpha. The paper introduces log-Korobov spaces to obtain precise endpoint estimates for alpha arbitrarily close to 1/2 and shows lattice rules yield error bounds of order O(N^{-1/2} (log N)^{-mu(1-lambda)/2}), with tractability results for weighted Korobov spaces under refined conditions on product weights.

citations.claim: QMC rules are equal weight quadrature rules for approximating integrals over $[0,1]^s$. One line of research studies the integration error of functions in the unit ball of so-called Korobov spaces, which are Hilbert spaces of periodic functions on $[0,1]^s$ with square integrable partial mixed derivatives of order $\alpha$.

To obtain such estimates we introduce a $\log$-scale for functions with smoothness close to $1/2$, which we call $\log$-Korobov spaces. We show that lattice rules can be used to obtain an integration error of order $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2} (\log N)^{-\mu(1-\lambda)/2})$ for any $1/\mu < \lambda \le 1$.

We also consider tractability of numerical integration for weighted Korobov spaces with product weights $(\gamma_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$. In this paper we give a more refined estimate for the case where $\tau$ is close to $1/(2 \alpha)$, namely we show dimension independent error bounds under the condition that $\sum_{j=1}^\infty \gamma_j \max\{1, \log \gamma_j^{-1}\}^{\mu(1-\lambda)} < \infty$ for some $1/\mu < \lambda \le 1$.

balanced.summary: QMC rules are equal-weight quadrature rules for approximating integrals over [0,1]^s. A line of research studies the integration error for functions in the unit ball of Korobov spaces, which are Hilbert spaces of periodic functions with square-integrable partial mixed derivatives of order alpha; using Parseval's identity, smoothness is defined for alpha > 1/2. Doc_1 introduces log-Korobov spaces to obtain refined endpoint estimates for alpha close to 1/2, showing lattice rules give error O(N^{-1/2} (log N)^{-\mu(1-\lambda)/2}) for certain parameters, and gives tractability results for weighted Korobov spaces as well as extensions to log-cosine spaces. Related work includes explicit construction of optimal-order QMC rules in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of smooth functions (doc_2) and a Hilbert-space worst-case error/discrepancy relation (doc_8).

citations.claim: QMC rules are equal weight quadrature rules for approximating integrals over [0,1]^s; one line of research studies the integration error of functions in the unit ball of Korobov spaces, which are Hilbert spaces of periodic functions with square integrable partial mixed derivatives of order alpha, defined for all real alpha > 1/2 via Parseval's identity.

The paper introduces log-Korobov spaces to obtain endpoint estimates for smoothness close to 1/2, showing that lattice rules yield integration error of order O(N^{-1/2} (log N)^{-\mu(1-\lambda)/2}) for any 1/\mu < lambda <= 1, and gives dimension-independent error bounds for weighted Korobov spaces under conditions involving product weights; the results also apply to log-cosine spaces using tent-transformed lattice rules.

There exists a quasi-Monte Carlo rule which achieves the best possible rate of convergence for numerical integration in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space consisting of smooth functions, and an explicit construction is given using digit interlacing and digital nets with large minimum Hamming and Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman metrics.

Stolarsky's invariance principle can be read as expressing the worst-case numerical integration error for functions from the unit ball in a Hilbert space in terms of the L2-discrepancy and vice versa, and the note gives a simple proof using reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.

standard.summary: Vortex element methods are Lagrangian techniques often used to efficiently simulate incompressible flows. The Fast Multipole Method (FMM) considerably speeds up both velocity evaluation and vorticity evolution terms. A formulation based on the Lamb-Helmholtz decomposition can reduce the computations to just two scalar harmonic FMM sums, improving efficiency. FMM-based vortex methods have also been implemented on GPUs, though a comparison with a spectral method for isotropic turbulence showed the spectral method to be faster in that specific setup.

citations.claim: Vortex element methods are often used to efficiently simulate incompressible flows using Lagrangian techniques, and use of the FMM allows considerable speed up of both velocity evaluation and vorticity evolution terms.

Using the Lamb-Helmholtz decomposition, extremely efficient vortex element computations can be made, needing evaluation of just two scalar harmonic FMM sums for evaluating the velocity and vorticity evolution terms.
The Lagrangian vortex method uses the fast multipole method (FMM) as its numerical engine, and an FMM code (exaFMM) runs on GPU hardware using CUDA.

Results indicate that, for decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence, the spectral method is an order of magnitude faster than the vortex method when using a single GPU for the FMM and six CPU cores for the FFT.

balanced.summary: Vortex element methods are Lagrangian techniques for incompressible flow simulation; the Fast Multipole Method (FMM) considerably speeds up both velocity evaluation and vorticity evolution, and a Lamb-Helmholtz formulation reduces the required work to two scalar harmonic FMM sums. Lagrangian vortex-particle methods are also used for two-phase flow and fluid-rigid body coupling, and vorticity is well suited for particle flow-map evolution, though some approaches reconstruct velocity on a grid. GPU-accelerated FMM implementations exist for vortex methods, but comparisons with pseudo-spectral DNS show the spectral method can be faster for certain homogeneous turbulence cases. Related flow-map and particle-regularization techniques provide additional advances in resolution and speed.

citations.claim: Vortex element methods are often used to efficiently simulate incompressible flows using Lagrangian techniques, and FMM accelerates both velocity evaluation and vorticity evolution terms.
A Lamb-Helmholtz decomposition formulation requires evaluation of just two scalar harmonic FMM sums for velocity and vorticity evolution, instead of several scalar sums.
The Lagrangian vortex method uses the FMM as numerical engine, making it a potential candidate for exascale systems, with GPU implementations such as exaFMM.
In a comparison for decaying homogeneous isotropic turbulence on a 256^3 grid, the pseudo-spectral method was an order of magnitude faster than the vortex method for the tested implementations.
A Lagrangian method based on vortex particles, level-sets, and immersed boundary methods can simulate bi-phasic flow and fluid-rigid body coupling with local precision and efficiency.
Vorticity is an ideal quantity for evolution on particle flow maps, and the VPFM method evolves vorticity on particles while reconstructing velocity on a background grid.
Vorticity is preferable to impulse for flow-map-based vortex methods due to numerical stability and physical interpretability.
The characteristic mapping method, a semi-Lagrangian method, evolves the flow map and offers exponential resolution to resolve fine-scale vortex sheet structures.
Smooth partition-of-unity finite element spaces for vortex particle regularization can produce significant speed-ups when the grid spacing is proportional to the square-root of particle spacing.

citations.claim: The prevalence of ocular illnesses is growing globally, presenting a substantial public health challenge; early detection and timely intervention are crucial for averting visual impairment and enhancing patient prognosis, and the proposed CELD framework achieved 91% accuracy on fundus image classification.

Foundation vision-language models like ChatGPT-4o and medical VLMs markedly underperform practicing ophthalmologists on tasks crucial to age-related macular degeneration care, while a curriculum-trained model, RetinaVLM, improved disease staging (F1 0.63 vs 0.33) and patient referral (0.67 vs 0.50).

In an AMD diagnosis workflow, AI assistance enhanced diagnostic accuracy for 23 of 24 clinicians (average F1-score +20%) and reduced diagnostic times for 17 of 19 clinicians, with up to 40% time savings.

Retinal imaging provides an opportunity for early detection, monitoring of disease progression and intervention for both ocular and non-ocular diseases, with AI-driven analysis bridging the eye and systemic health.

Vision-threatening eye diseases pose a major global health burden, with timely diagnosis limited by workforce shortages and restricted access to specialized care; a multimodal benchmark of 32,633 instances was created to advance ophthalmic AI.

For diseases like AMD, DME, and RVO treated with IVOM, predicting visual acuity and detecting deterioration under real-life conditions is challenging due to heterogeneous and incomplete data; a multistage system achieved 69% macro F1-score for VA progression prediction.

VisionFM, a foundation model pre-trained on 3.4 million ophthalmic images, supports disease screening, diagnosis, prognosis, and systemic biomarker prediction, outperforming basic and intermediate-level ophthalmologists in jointly diagnosing 12 common ophthalmic diseases.

standard.summary: The proposed approach is an innovative two-headed attention layer called Geometric-Latent attention (Ge-Latto) that combines geometric and latent features to segment 3D scenes into semantically meaningful subsets. Each head uses either geometric or latent features of a local neighborhood and combines local and global information to learn better local relationships. The method is permutation-invariant via shared-MLP layers and robust to varying point cloud densities because the local attention layer does not depend on neighbor order. It achieves competitive results on ShapeNetPart and ModelNet40 and state-of-the-art segmentation on S3DIS with 69.2% IoU on Area 5 and 89.7% overall accuracy under K-fold cross-validation.

citations.claim: We present an innovative two-headed attention layer that combines geometric and latent features to segment a 3D scene into semantically meaningful subsets. Each head combines local and global information, using either the geometric or latent features, of a neighborhood of points and uses this information to learn better local relationships.

Our method is invariant to permutation thanks to the use of shared-MLP layers, and it can also be used with point clouds with varying densities because the local attention layer does not depend on the neighbor order.

Our proposal is simple yet robust, which allows it to achieve competitive results in the ShapeNetPart and ModelNet40 datasets, and the state-of-the-art when segmenting the complex dataset S3DIS, with 69.2% IoU on Area 5, and 89.7% overall accuracy using K-fold cross-validation on the 6 areas.

balanced.summary: The query describes an innovative headed attention layer that combines geometric and latent features to segment a 3D scene into semantically meaningful subsets, with each head fusing local and global information. This matches the Geometric-Latent attention layer (Ge-Latto) presented in doc_1, which uses two heads—one for geometric features and one for latent features—on a neighborhood of points, and couples this with a sub-sampling strategy to capture global features. Ge-Latto is permutation invariant, robust to varying point densities, and achieves state-of-the-art segmentation on S3DIS. Related work in doc_3 also explores local-global attention for point cloud segmentation by fusing density-aware local attention with global attention to improve small-object handling, while doc_4 proposes a feature-boosting network with channel attention for scene parsing that gathers spatial context from multiple feature levels. These works collectively illustrate the use of multi-head attention and local-global fusion for semantic scene segmentation.

citations.claim: Presents an innovative two-headed attention layer that combines geometric and latent features to segment a 3D scene into semantically meaningful subsets, with each head combining local and global information using either geometric or latent features of a neighborhood of points.

The Geometric-Latent attention layer (Ge-Latto) is combined with a sub-sampling strategy to capture global features, is permutation invariant via shared-MLP layers, and handles point clouds with varying densities because the local attention layer does not depend on neighbor order.

Proposes a point cloud segmentation network that fuses local attention based on density perception with global attention, increasing the effective receptive field of each point while reducing information loss about small objects in dense areas.

Presents a feature-boosting network for scene parsing that gathers spatial context from multiple levels of feature extraction and computes attention weights for each level to generate final class labels, using a channel attention module to boost relevant features.

standard.summary: Financial recommendation systems commonly neglect behavioral and regulatory factors, which produces advice misaligned with user preferences, hard to interpret, and unlikely to be followed. To address this, FLARKO combines large language models, knowledge graphs, and Kahneman-Tversky Optimization to generate asset recommendations that are both profitable and behaviorally aligned, with interpretable context from structured knowledge graphs and strong performance on behavioral alignment and joint profitability.

citations.claim: Most financial recommendation systems often fail to account for key behavioral and regulatory factors, leading to advice that is misaligned with user preferences, difficult to interpret, or unlikely to be followed.
FLARKO integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), Knowledge Graphs (KGs), and Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) to generate asset recommendations that are both profitable and behaviorally aligned.
FLARKO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art recommendation baselines on behavioral alignment and joint profitability, while remaining interpretable and resource-efficient.

balanced.summary: Financial recommendation systems often fail to incorporate key behavioral and regulatory factors, resulting in advice that is misaligned with user preferences, hard to interpret, and unlikely to be followed; the FLARKO framework addresses these gaps by integrating large language models, knowledge graphs, and Kahneman-Tversky optimization to produce behaviorally aligned, interpretable, and profitable asset recommendations. Broader evidence reinforces that user trust and acceptance depend on factors such as robo-advisor performance framing, credibility signals, and interpretability of algorithmic outputs, while systemic biases and cybersecurity risks also complicate financial advice and retention systems.

citations.claim: Most financial recommendation systems often fail to account for key behavioral and regulatory factors, leading to advice that is misaligned with user preferences, difficult to interpret, or unlikely to be followed; FLARKO integrates LLMs, knowledge graphs, and KTO to generate profitable and behaviorally aligned recommendations.

GPT's financial literacy varies by model version, with GPT-4 achieving near-perfect performance, suggesting that financial literacy is an emergent ability of state-of-the-art large language models and requiring research on how people use them as advice sources.

People tend to rely on robo-advisors, with reliance shaped by information about RA performance and the framing of advice as gains or losses, and thematic analysis reveals distinct roles and user types in advice integration.

Crypto Key Opinion Leaders' credibility is a self-determined, ethically enacted practice marked by self-regulation, bounded epistemic competence, accountability, and reflexive self-correction, with implications for designing credibility signals that prioritize transparency.

Traditional investment recommendations focus on high-return stocks or highly diversified portfolios, often neglecting user preferences, and the proposed MVECF model optimally blends user preference with portfolio theory to improve mean-variance efficiency.

A/B experiment metrics obtained during transition periods after changing a recommendation algorithm are biased indicators of the system's long-term performance due to user inflow, churn, and retention dynamics, potentially yielding false conclusions.

Many contemporary churn models operate as opaque black boxes, and a three-component framework integrating explainable AI, survival analysis, and RFM profiling enables attribution of churn drivers, estimation of intervention windows, and prioritization of customer segments.

Phishing and malware remain the most commonly exploited cyber threats in digital banking, while multi-factor authentication, biometric security, AI-driven fraud detection, and regulatory compliance enhance security but third-party FinTech integration introduces additional risks.

standard.summary: In high energy physics, machine learning methods typically rely on large volumes of precise simulation for training. As these models become more complex, they become increasingly sensitive to differences between simulation and real experimental data.

citations.claim: The use of machine learning methods in high energy physics typically relies on large volumes of precise simulation for training. As machine learning models become more complex they can become increasingly sensitive to differences between this simulation and the real data collected by experiments.

balanced.summary: High-energy physics (HEP) machine learning typically depends on large volumes of precise simulation for training, and as models become more complex they grow increasingly sensitive to differences between simulation and real data [doc_1]. A contrastive-learning approach, MACK, mitigates this mismodeling without needing prior knowledge of its specifics [doc_1]. Similarly, re-simulation-based self-supervised learning (RS3L) creates augmentations by intervening in stochastic simulators, enabling robust representations for downstream tasks such as object discrimination and uncertainty mitigation [doc_6]. Beyond these HEP-specific solutions, the broader field of physics-enhanced ML addresses limited informative data, accurate-but-wrong predictions, and uncertainty [doc_3]; physics-consistent ML projects outputs onto physical manifolds to enforce compliance with physical laws [doc_5]; and physics-informed kernel learning provides theoretical guarantees when integrating PDE priors [doc_8]. Large-scale simulation collections such as the Well support training and benchmarking across diverse physical systems [doc_4]. These methods collectively improve the reliability of simulation-trained models when confronted with real experimental data.

citations.claim: The use of machine learning methods in high energy physics typically relies on large volumes of precise simulation for training; as models become more complex they become increasingly sensitive to differences between simulation and real data.

A generic methodology based on contrastive learning is able to greatly mitigate the negative effect of simulation-real mismodeling without requiring prior knowledge of the specifics of the mismodeling.

RS3L is a novel simulation-based SSL strategy that employs re-simulation to drive data augmentation for contrastive learning, generating multiple realizations of an event in stochastic simulators; pre-training with RS3L enables powerful performance in downstream tasks such as discrimination of objects and uncertainty mitigation.

The need to go beyond machine learning strategies is driven by limited volume of informative data, avoiding accurate-but-wrong predictions, dealing with uncertainties, and providing explainable and interpretable inferences.

A novel physics-consistent machine learning method directly enforces compliance with physical principles by projecting model outputs onto the manifold defined by these laws, ensuring predictions inherently adhere to constraints and improving reliability and interpretability.

Physics-informed kernel learning (PIKL) minimizes a physics-informed risk function using Fourier methods, provides theoretical guarantees on the physical prior's impact on convergence speed, and can outperform physics-informed neural networks in accuracy and computation time.

The Well is a large-scale collection of 15TB of data across 16 datasets covering diverse physical domains, with a unified PyTorch interface, to facilitate training and evaluating machine learning surrogate models.

standard.summary: Timing and burst patterns can leak through encryption, and an adaptive adversary can exploit them, which undermines metadata-only detection on a stand-alone consumer gateway. Therefore, consumer gateways need streaming intrusion detection on encrypted traffic using metadata only, under tight CPU and latency budgets. A proposed solution, NOS-Gate, implements lightweight per-flow scoring and achieves high incident recall at a low false-positive rate while keeping scoring cost small in CPU time.

citations.claim: Timing and burst patterns can leak through encryption, and an adaptive adversary can exploit them.
This undermines metadata-only detection in a stand-alone consumer gateway.
Consumer gateways need streaming intrusion detection on encrypted traffic using metadata only, under tight CPU and latency budgets.

NOS-Gate attains 0.952 incident recall versus 0.857 for the best baseline at a 0.1% false-positive operating point, and reduces p99.9 queueing delay and collateral delay with a mean scoring cost of about 2.09 microseconds per flow-window on CPU.

balanced.summary: Timing and burst patterns can leak through encryption, and an adaptive adversary can exploit them, undermining metadata-only detection at a stand-alone consumer gateway. This makes streaming intrusion detection on encrypted traffic using only metadata necessary under tight CPU and latency budgets, as implemented by NOS-Gate, a lightweight two-state spiking unit per flow that scores fixed-length metadata-feature windows, applies a K-of-M persistence rule, and triggers reversible WFQ-based mitigation; it achieves 0.952 incident recall at 0.1% false positives versus 0.857 for the best baseline, reduces p99.9 queueing and collateral delay, and costs about 2.09 microseconds per flow-window. Related work reinforces the importance of temporal and inter-flow signals for encrypted-traffic detection: inter-flow signals capturing temporal correlations generalize across classification tasks; NetFlow datasets with temporal features reveal unique attack patterns; flow-correlation attacks on Tor show that traffic patterns leak despite encryption; many ML classifiers suffer from legacy datasets and overfitting; LLM instruction tuning can handle non-I.I.D. encrypted traffic; handshake attributes can identify user platforms; and future programmable data planes can embed distributed ML-based intrusion prevention. Together, these results point to metadata-only, streaming, resource-aware defenses that are robust to timing-controlled evasion.

citations.claim: Timing and burst patterns can leak through encryption, and an adaptive adversary can exploit them, undermining metadata-only detection in a stand-alone consumer gateway; consumer gateways therefore need streaming intrusion detection on encrypted traffic using metadata only under tight CPU and latency budgets.

NOS-Gate, a streaming IDS for stand-alone gateways, uses a lightweight two-state unit from Network-Optimised Spiking dynamics per flow, scores fixed-length windows of metadata features, and under a K-of-M persistence rule triggers reversible mitigation that temporarily reduces the flow's weight under weighted fair queueing; at 0.1% false-positive operating point it attains 0.952 incident recall versus 0.857 for the best baseline, reduces p99.9 queueing delay and collateral delay, with mean scoring cost of about 2.09 microseconds per flow-window.

A generalizable encrypted traffic classification model operating on raw PCAP data uses inter-flow signals, an innovative representation that captures temporal correlations and packet volume distributions across flows, outperforming well-established methods and achieving up to 99% accuracy.

ML-based encrypted network traffic classifiers often rely on outdated datasets and mistakenly utilize unencrypted traffic due to legacy datasets; feature occlusion experiments show oversights in design choices lead to overfitting, and unsubstantiated assumptions impact real-world applicability.

Tor is vulnerable to flow correlation attacks that deanonymize users by correlating traffic patterns from ingress and egress segments, showing that encrypted traffic patterns can still leak and be exploited.

Temporal NetFlow features such as inter-packet arrival time and flow length/duration are critical for ML-based NIDS; time-frequency signal presentations show that many attacks have unique patterns that can help ML models identify them more easily.

Encrypted traffic classification faces distribution drift and label scarcity; ETooL integrates LLMs with traffic-structure knowledge through self-supervised instruction tuning, achieving robust classification and superior generalization in supervised and zero-shot tasks, with notable F1-score improvements on I.I.D., O.O.D., and botnet datasets.

Despite encryption and NAT limiting ISP visibility, user platforms for video streams can be identified by analyzing TCP/QUIC and TLS handshake anatomy; a classification pipeline using 62 handshake attributes achieves over 96% accuracy in determining user device and software agent.

Future programmable data planes can give devices anomaly detection capabilities and cooperate in a fully distributed fashion as an ML-enabled intrusion prevention system embedded in the network, working effectively while occupying less CPU and RAM resources.

standard.summary: The work proposes an upscaling method for nonlinear Forchheimer flow in highly heterogeneous porous media. It considers the generalized Forchheimer law for incompressible and slightly compressible single-phase flows, expresses the system as a degenerate nonlinear flow equation for pressure, and determines coarse-scale parameters by matching the volumetric average of velocity between fine and coarse scales. The approach combines recent analytical results with rigorous mathematical upscaling theory for monotone operators, and includes analytical upscaling formulas for stratified domains that correlate well with numerical results.

citations.claim: In this work we propose upscaling method for nonlinear Forchheimer flow in highly heterogeneous porous media. The generalized Forchheimer law is considered for incompressible and slightly-compressible single-phase flows.
The coarse scale parameters for the steady state problem are determined so that the volumetric average of velocity of the flow in the domain on fine scale and on coarse scale are close enough.

Compared to previous works Durlofsky and Karimi-Fard (2009) and Peszynska et al. (2009), our approach relies on recent analytical results of Aulisa et al. (2009) and combines it with rigorous mathematical upscaling theory for monotone operators.
Analytical upscaling formulas in stratified domain are obtained for the nonlinear case. They correlate with high accuracy with numerical results.

balanced.summary: The proposed upscaling method for nonlinear Forchheimer flow in highly heterogeneous porous media is presented in doc_1. It considers the generalized Forchheimer law for incompressible and slightly compressible single-phase flows, rewrites the system via analytical results as a degenerate nonlinear pressure equation, and calibrates coarse-scale parameters by matching volumetric average velocity between fine and coarse scales. The equivalent permeability tensor is first evaluated using linear-case streamlines and then modified to capture nonlinear effects; analytical upscaling formulas for stratified domains show high accuracy against numerical results. Other documents address related but distinct challenges: doc_2 proposes nonlinear model reduction with GMsFEM and empirical interpolation, doc_3 develops an adaptive multiscale solver for compressible flows, doc_6 uses online mixed multiscale methods with oversampling for heterogeneous media, and doc_10 introduces a two-grid preconditioner with an adaptive coarse space for flow simulations in highly heterogeneous media.

citations.claim: This work proposes an upscaling method for nonlinear Forchheimer flow in highly heterogeneous porous media, considering the generalized Forchheimer law for incompressible and slightly-compressible single-phase flows.

The coarse scale parameters are determined so that the volumetric average of velocity on fine and coarse scales are close, using a flow-based coarsening approach where equivalent permeability tensor is evaluated following linear cases and modified for nonlinear effects.
Analytical upscaling formulas in stratified domains are obtained for the nonlinear case and correlate with high accuracy with numerical results.
Related nonlinear model reduction for flows in heterogeneous porous media uses GMsFEM and empirical interpolation to reduce computational complexity while capturing fully-resolved solutions.
Another approach, C-AMS, provides an adaptive algebraic multiscale solver for compressible flow in heterogeneous porous media, with basis function formulations and adaptive operator updates.
Online mixed multiscale finite element methods with oversampling are extended for flow problems in highly heterogeneous porous media, including steady-state and two-phase flow.
A two-grid preconditioner with adaptive spectral coarse space is designed for flow simulations in highly heterogeneous media, tested for Darcy and two-phase flow.

standard.summary: The study addresses a continuous-time Bayesian quickest detection problem where observation times are a scarce resource, and an agent is limited to making a finite number of discrete observations while adaptively deciding the observation strategy to minimize detection delay and false alarm probability. The paper establishes the existence of optimal strategies under two models of observation rights, develops an algorithmic approach via jump operators, provides numerical illustrations, and proves convergence to Shiryaev's classical continuous-observation problem as the number of observation rights tends to infinity.

citations.claim: We study a continuous time Bayesian quickest detection problem in which observation times are a scarce resource. The agent, limited to making a finite number of discrete observations, must adaptively decide his observation strategy to minimize detection delay and the probability of false alarm.
Under two different models of observation rights, we establish the existence of optimal strategies, and formulate an algorithmic approach to the problem via jump operators.
We describe algorithms for these problems, and illustrate them with some numerical results.
As the number of observation rights tends to infinity, we also show convergence to the classical continuous observation problem of Shiryaev.

balanced.summary: This paper studies a continuous-time Bayesian quickest detection problem in which observation times are a scarce resource; the agent, limited to making a finite number of discrete observations, must adaptively decide his observation strategy to minimize detection delay and the probability of false alarm. Under two different models of observation rights, the existence of optimal strategies is established, and an algorithmic approach via jump operators is formulated, with numerical illustrations. As the number of observation rights tends to infinity, the problem converges to the classical continuous observation problem of Shiryaev. This work fits within a broader literature on resource-constrained quickest change detection, including reviews of multi-stream QCD with sampling limitations, and relates to adaptive sensing in mixed observability domains and finite-horizon sequential sensing.

citations.claim: We study a continuous time Bayesian quickest detection problem in which observation times are a scarce resource.
The agent, limited to making a finite number of discrete observations, must adaptively decide his observation strategy to minimize detection delay and the probability of false alarm.
Under two different models of observation rights, we establish the existence of optimal strategies, and formulate an algorithmic approach to the problem via jump operators.
As the number of observation rights tends to infinity, we also show convergence to the classical continuous observation problem of Shiryaev.
we discuss sampling constraints, where observations must be selected or acquired sequentially under resource limitations.

Sequential decision making under uncertainty is studied in a mixed observability domain. The goal is to maximize the amount of information obtained on a partially observable stochastic process under constraints imposed by a fully observable internal state.

The objective is a sequential strategy governing the decision of sensing and exploitation at each time to maximize the expected utility (i.e., total reward minus total penalty and sensing cost) over a finite horizon.

standard.summary: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) can benefit from robots' ability to interpret human emotional states, but current emotion recognition (ER) models in HRC often fall short, particularly because they rely on acted datasets and single-modality inputs such as facial expressions. A proposed vision language model (VLM)-based ER system leverages contextual understanding to improve emotion interpretation in HRC, achieving higher semantic similarity and positive sentiment alignment with human annotations compared to a baseline CNN-based system, and users preferred the resulting emotion-adaptive robot behavior.

citations.claim: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) can benefit from robots' abilities to interpret human emotional states, but current emotion recognition (ER) models in HRC often fall short, particularly due to their reliance on acted datasets and single-modality inputs like facial expressions.

A proposed VLM-ER system leverages contextual understanding and achieves higher semantic similarity and positive sentiment alignment with human annotations compared to a baseline convolutional neural network-based system; participants preferred emotion-adaptive robot behavior facilitated by the VLM-ER system.

balanced.summary: Human-robot collaboration can be enhanced when robots interpret human emotional states, but current emotion recognition (ER) models are limited because they often rely on acted datasets and single-modality inputs such as facial expressions (doc_1). Contextual understanding—including body pose, scene context, and commonsense reasoning—is essential for accurate apparent emotion recognition, and large vision language models offer a promising path beyond traditional baselines (doc_10). In HRC settings, monitoring physiological signals (e.g., ECG, GSR, pupillometry) can estimate comfort and discomfort, enabling robots to adapt to the human's psycho-physiological state (doc_4). Additionally, research on robot emotional expression shows that robot behavior can influence human attention, stress, preference, and emotional experience in interaction (doc_3), and that emotionally expressive robots can shape children's behavior in cooperative tasks (doc_5). However, emotion perception is not trivial: recognition accuracy declines when only partial facial information is available, and robot appearance affects emotion recognition (doc_2). Robots can also defuse high-intensity conflicts by acknowledging the situation and expressing remorse across multiple modalities (doc_8). Theoretical work suggests emotions can be understood as recognized patterns of cognitive activities, which may help bridge diverse emotion theories for computational implementation (doc_9). Together, these studies indicate that improving ER in HRC requires moving beyond acted, single-modality approaches toward context-aware, multi-modal, and physiologically grounded methods.

citations.claim: HRC can benefit from robots' abilities to interpret human emotional states, but current ER models in HRC often fall short due to reliance on acted datasets and single-modality inputs like facial expressions; a VLM-based ER system leveraging contextual understanding improves emotion interpretation.

Facial expressions are not enough for emotion recognition; body pose, contextual knowledge, and commonsense reasoning contribute, and fine-tuned vision language models significantly outperform traditional baselines on the EMOTIC dataset.

Fluent human-robot collaboration requires a robot teammate to understand and adapt to the human's psycho-physiological state; the study estimates comfortability/uncomfortability indices from physiological signals (ECG, GSR, pupillometry).

Emotionally expressive motion patterns of a follower robot significantly shift the human operator's attention, emotional state, and overall experience; angry behavior heightened stress and was least preferred, while happy behavior was most preferred.
Children aligned their behavior to a robot's inferred emotional state in a cooperative game, but higher levels of expressiveness did not result in increased alignment.

Recognition accuracy of emotional expressions in both humans and robots declines when only the eye region is visible, and robots with more human-like features enhance emotion recognition when only the eye region is shown.

All tested affective expression modalities can successfully defuse high-intensity conflict situations by conveying acknowledgment of the confrontation and remorse, indicating social awareness matters more than special expression abilities.

Emotions are proposed as recognized patterns of cognitive activities that arise from deviations between goal targets and action performances, linking emotions to attention and cognitive architecture parameters.

standard.summary: The effect of preconditioning linear weighted least-squares using an approximation of the model matrix is analyzed, revealing the interplay of the eigenstructures of both the model and weighting matrices. A small example demonstrates the potential inefficiency of such preconditioners.

standard.summary: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a heuristic hybrid quantum-classical method for combinatorial optimization problems. It has been demonstrated to scale better than state-of-the-art classical solvers in some settings: QAOA-based methods achieve high-quality solutions faster on very large graphs, and a related quantum algorithm for 0-1 knapsack offers competitive or better runtimes than classical solvers. However, such advantages are not universal: QAOA may require exponential time for linear functions when the number of layers is below a threshold, and lower bounds show that many rounds are needed to guarantee constant approximation ratios for most problems. Moreover, performance depends heavily on the specific problem instance and on parameter settings; parameter transfer and solver selection must be tailored to the instance.

citations.claim: QAOA is one of the most promising quantum heuristics for combinatorial optimization; it has been shown to perform well on small-scale instances and to provide an asymptotic speedup over state-of-the-art classical algorithms for some problems, though fault tolerance is required to realize this speedup in practice.

A multilevel QAOA reinforced with graph representation learning, called MLQAOA, demonstrates the potential of using multilevel QAOA and representation learning on very large graphs by achieving high-quality solutions in a much faster time.

The Quantum Tree Generator for 0-1 knapsack problems offers competitive runtimes compared to classical state-of-the-art solvers already for instances involving as few as 100 variables, indicating potential practical quantum advantage for large-scale problems.
QAOA requires exponential time to solve linear functions when the number of layers p is less than the number of different coefficients n, and the runtime is linear only if p is at least n.
Lower bounds show that QAOA with Grover-style mixing requires at least a polynomial number of rounds to guarantee any constant approximation ratio for most problems.
The performance of QAOA depends crucially on the choice of the free parameters in the circuit.

Optimal QAOA parameters from one instance can be transferred to another, but a selective layer optimization scheme offers a favorable trade-off between solution quality and computational time, and the approximation ratio scales with problem size.

Selecting the best solver for an optimization problem depends heavily on the problem itself; a predictive machine-learning approach selects the best solver in more than 70% of cases and a solver in the top two in about 90% of problems.

balanced.summary: QAOA is a leading heuristic for combinatorial optimization that can in principle provide asymptotic speedups over state-of-the-art classical algorithms for some problems, but practical demonstrations remain limited and performance depends strongly on the problem instance and parameter choices. Hardware demonstrations have scaled QAOA to N·p up to 320 for MaxCut on non-planar 3-regular graphs, and hybrid variants such as MLQAOA report faster high-quality solutions on very large graphs. At the same time, theoretical lower bounds indicate that QAOA needs at least polynomial rounds to guarantee constant approximation ratios for most problems and can require exponential time for linear functions when the number of layers is below the number of distinct coefficients. Empirical studies also show instance-dependent behavior, e.g., outperforming classical genetic algorithms in only some test-case optimization instances, and parameter transfer/selection techniques depend on instance size and characteristics.

citations.claim: QAOA is a promising quantum heuristic for combinatorial optimization with asymptotic speedup over state-of-the-art classical algorithms for some problems, but its performance depends crucially on free parameter choices and fault tolerance is required to realize the speedup.
QAOA was executed for MaxCut on non-planar 3-regular graphs with N·p up to 320 on Quantinuum H1-1 and H2 trapped-ion processors, the highest N·p demonstrated on hardware to date.
MLQAOA combines multilevel algorithms with graph representation learning and QAOA/QAOA-inspired solvers, achieving high-quality solutions on very large graphs in much faster time.
Lower bounds show that QAOA with Grover-style mixers requires at least a polynomial number of rounds to guarantee any constant approximation ratio for most problems.
QAOA requires exponential time to solve linear functions when the number of layers p is less than the number of different coefficients n, with linear runtime only if p ≥ n.

In empirical evaluation on five test case optimization problems, IGDec-QAOA reached the same effectiveness as GA and outperformed GA in only two of the five problems, showing instance-dependent performance.

Optimal QAOA parameters from one Max-Cut instance can transfer to another instance, and selective layer optimization offers a trade-off between solution quality and computational time, with performance scaling depending on problem size.

The best quantum solver for an optimization problem depends heavily on the problem itself; a predictive machine-learning approach selected the best solver in over 70% of cases and a top-two solver in about 90% of 500+ QUBO problems.

standard.summary: The query highlights the problem of fake news dissemination on social media and the research effort to limit its diffusion. A promising approach is link deletion in social networks; however, empirical evaluation using real retweet cascades shows that deleting 10%-50% of links reduces cascade size to only about 50% of the original under optimistic estimates, indicating limited effectiveness and inefficiency for cascades with many seed users. Other interventions show more promise: attaching fact-checking notes (Community Notes) significantly reduces engagement and diffusion, with reductions of 46.1% in reposts, 44.1% in likes, 21.9% in replies, and 13.5% in views after attachment. Research also reveals that misinformation often repurposes reliable sources via co-sharing, that users adopt low-credibility sources with fewer exposures than high-credibility ones, and that large language models enable simulation of fake news propagation to evaluate intervention strategies. Overall, the literature underscores the need for multifaceted approaches beyond simple link deletion.

citations.claim: Link deletion methods have been shown effective in reducing diffusion cascades in synthetic models, but empirical evaluation with real retweet cascades shows that deleting 10%-50% of links only reduces cascade size to about 50% under optimistic estimates, and many cascades with many seed users render link deletion inefficient.

Community Notes fact-checking significantly reduces engagement with and diffusion of false content, resulting in reductions of 46.1% in reposts, 44.1% in likes, 21.9% in replies, and 13.5% in views after being attached.

Articles from reliable sources that are co-shared with fake news are significantly more likely to contain misleading narratives, consistent with users using mainstream information to enhance credibility and reach of potentially misleading claims.
Users tend to adopt low-credibility sources with fewer exposures than high-credibility sources, and the number of exposures needed for adoption varies based on source credibility.

A Fake news Propagation Simulation framework (FPS) based on large language models uncovers patterns in fake news propagation related to topic relevance and individual traits, and demonstrates that early and appropriately frequent interventions balance governance cost and effectiveness.

balanced.summary: Social media hosts beneficial information but also harmful fake news, prompting extensive research on limiting its diffusion. Link deletion is highlighted as a promising approach, yet empirical evaluation using actual retweet cascades shows that deleting 10%–50% of links reduces cascade size to only about 50% of the original under optimistic estimates, suggesting limited effectiveness [doc_1]. Other interventions also show promise: Community Notes fact-checking significantly reduces engagement with and diffusion of false content [doc_9]; rumor detection and source detection are studied jointly to identify and block misinformation [doc_3]; LLM-based simulations of fake news propagation indicate that early and appropriately frequent interventions balance governance cost and effectiveness [doc_4]; and empirical frameworks reveal that users adopt low-credibility sources after fewer exposures than high-credibility ones [doc_5]. Research also models truth dissemination as a volunteer's dilemma where public contributions such as news subscriptions can help truth dominate fake news [doc_7], warns that LLM-generated fake news can cause 'truth decay' in neural news recommendation systems [doc_8], and shows that articles from reliable sources are often co-shared with fake news to advance misleading narratives [doc_2].

citations.claim: Link deletion is a promising approach to limiting harmful information diffusion, but empirical evaluation using actual retweet cascades shows that deleting 10%–50% of links reduces cascade size to only about 50% under optimistic estimation, indicating limited effectiveness.

Community Notes fact-checking significantly reduces engagement with and diffusion of false content, with average reductions of 46.1% in reposts, 44.1% in likes, 21.9% in replies, and 13.5% in views after being attached.

Rumor detection and rumor source detection are important for identifying and mitigating false information, and a comprehensive survey addresses these two problems jointly to understand their similarities and differences.

A Fake news Propagation Simulation framework based on large language models shows that early and appropriately frequent interventions strike a balance between governance cost and effectiveness in controlling fake news spread.

Users tend to adopt low-credibility sources with fewer exposures than high-credibility sources, and exposure to unreliable information increases the likelihood of adoption, even among non-partisan users.

The conflict between truth and fake news dissemination can be modeled as a volunteer's dilemma, and public contribution through news subscription (shared rewards) can impact the dominance of truth over fake news in the network.

LLM-generated fake news can induce truth decay in neural news recommendation systems, where real news gradually loses its advantageous ranking position against fake news as LLM-generated news is involved.

Articles from reliable sources that are frequently co-shared with fake news are significantly more likely to contain narratives present in misinformation content, suggesting mainstream information can be repurposed to advance misleading narratives.

standard.summary: Machine learning (ML) is becoming integral to cyber-physical systems (CPS), and there is a growing shift from traditional cloud-based training to on-device processing (TinyML) driven by privacy and latency concerns. On-device training uses local data without sharing it over wireless links, enabling privacy-preserving computation and reducing latency, while distributed TinyML methods like RockNet demonstrate that ultra-low-power CPS devices can learn tasks from scratch with state-of-the-art accuracy. Federated learning is another distributed, privacy-oriented approach that trains models across decentralized sources without centralizing raw data.

citations.claim: As Machine Learning (ML) becomes integral to Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), there is growing interest in shifting training from traditional cloud-based to on-device processing (TinyML), for example, due to privacy and latency concerns.
On-device training allows models to be trained via local data without the need to share data over wireless links, thus enabling privacy-preserving computation by design.

RockNet is a TinyML method for ultra-low-power hardware that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in timeseries classification without offline pretraining, reducing memory, latency and energy consumption per device by up to 90% when scaling from one central device to 20 devices.

The integration of ML in CPS is complex due to real-time decision making, safety, reliability, device heterogeneity, and data privacy; federated learning is a distributed approach that trains models using data from decentralized sources.

balanced.summary: Machine learning (ML) is integral to cyber-physical systems (CPS), but its integration poses challenges such as real-time decision-making, safety, reliability, device heterogeneity, and data privacy. There is a growing shift from traditional cloud-based training toward on-device processing (TinyML), driven by privacy and latency concerns. Examples include distributed on-device training on ultra-low-power devices that cuts memory, latency, and energy use, as well as edge and in-network ML that enables low-latency inference and local data processing. Complementary approaches such as federated learning with differential privacy, secure confidential computing, and security-focused MLOps help balance privacy, accuracy, and security, while anomaly detection in CPS benefits from data-driven ML methods.

citations.claim: The integration of ML in CPS is complex due to challenges in real-time decision making, safety, reliability, device heterogeneity, and data privacy; federated learning allows models to be trained using data from decentralized sources.

As ML becomes integral to CPS, there is growing interest in shifting training from traditional cloud-based to on-device processing (TinyML) due to privacy and latency concerns; RockNet enables distributed training on ultra-low-power devices, reducing memory, latency, and energy consumption per device by up to 90%.

On-device training allows models to be trained via local data without sharing data over wireless links, enabling privacy-preserving computation by design, model personalization, and deployment in remote locations without stable internet connectivity.
Executing ML at the edge of IoT networks can enhance sustainability by reducing bandwidth usage, enabling real-time decision-making, and improving data privacy.
P4-programmable FPGA SmartNICs enable In-Network Machine Learning for low-latency inference tasks such as QoS prediction and anomaly detection, with retrainable models deployable at the network edge.

Federated learning preserves privacy by training ML models locally while transmitting only model updates; FedHDPrivacy actively monitors cumulative noise and adds only required differential privacy noise, surpassing standard federated learning frameworks by up to 37%.

The DP-HD framework combines explainable AI and hyperdimensional computing to quantify and predict noise effects on accuracy using a Signal-to-Noise Ratio metric, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy of 94.43% with robust privacy protections in additive manufacturing anomaly detection.

Anomaly detection is vital for preventing catastrophic failures in CPS; data-driven approaches such as machine learning and deep learning are among the categorized techniques for safer and more reliable systems.

SecMLOps provides a framework that integrates security throughout the MLOps lifecycle to safeguard against adversarial attacks, highlighting trade-offs between security measures and system performance.
Arm Confidential Computing Architecture (CCA) protects on-device ML models with at most 22% overhead across various applications and reduces membership inference attack success rate by 8.3%.

standard.summary: Cardiovascular hemodynamic fields provide valuable medical decision markers for coronary artery disease, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is the gold standard for accurate, non-invasive evaluation of these quantities in silico. Machine learning surrogate models can accelerate such hemodynamics estimation, and although invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) remains a physiologic gold standard, non-invasive ML-based FFR assessment is feasible and rapid.

citations.claim: Cardiovascular hemodynamic fields provide valuable medical decision markers for coronary artery disease; CFD is the gold standard for accurate, non-invasive evaluation of these quantities in silico.

Invasive FFR is a physiologic gold standard for assessing coronary stenosis severity, but the proposed attention-based multi-fidelity ML model enables non-invasive, rapid, and accurate FFR assessment.

balanced.summary: Cardiovascular hemodynamic fields are valuable decision markers for coronary artery disease, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is regarded as the gold standard for accurate, non-invasive in silico evaluation of these quantities. However, CFD can be computationally demanding, so machine-learning surrogates and integrated software tools are being developed to enable faster, non-invasive hemodynamic assessment while retaining accuracy. Complementary computational approaches also support hemodynamic modeling and uncertainty quantification, broadening the clinical applicability of such analyses.

citations.claim: Cardiovascular hemodynamic fields provide valuable medical decision markers for coronary artery disease, and CFD is the gold standard for accurate, non-invasive evaluation of these quantities in silico.
Invasive FFR is a physiologic gold standard for assessing coronary stenosis severity, and an attention-based multi-fidelity ML model enables non-invasive, rapid, and accurate FFR assessment.

An integrated open-source software system combines subject-specific MRI anatomy and CFD to generate and analyze blood flow simulations, facilitating hemodynamic analysis for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases.

FSGe strongly couples 3D Navier-Stokes blood flow with vascular growth and remodeling, capturing local wall shear stress variations that are important in localized disease processes such as atherosclerosis.
Metamodels for 0D cardiovascular models enable sensitivity analysis, parameter estimation, and uncertainty quantification, reducing the computational cost of repeated model evaluations.

standard.summary: Image saturation has affected several solar astronomy instruments, particularly at EUV wavelengths, and became a major big-data issue with the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) aboard the Solar Dynamic Observatory (SDO), involving on the order of 10^5 frames per year of the dataset provided since February 2010. A novel desaturation method can recover the signal in saturated regions of any AIA image using only information contained in the image itself, offering strong statistical reliability and suitability for a reconstruction pipeline for AIA data, including long-lasting, energetic flaring events.

citations.claim: Image saturation has been an issue for several instruments in solar astronomy, mainly at EUV wavelengths, and with the launch of AIA on SDO it became a big data issue involving around 10^5 frames per year of dataset since February 2010.

A novel desaturation method recovers the signal in saturated regions of any AIA image using only information contained in the image itself, and could serve as a reconstruction pipeline for AIA data even for long-lasting, very energetic flaring events.

balanced.summary: Image saturation is a recognized problem for solar instruments, especially at EUV wavelengths; with the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), saturation became a big-data issue affecting a massive number of frames since 2010. A proposed desaturation method recovers signal in saturated AIA images using only the image itself, supporting a possible reconstruction pipeline. Broader big-data challenges in solar and astronomical imaging are addressed through distributed data access (e.g., OSDF for Big Bear Solar Observatory), onboard image classification and compression for CubeSats with limited downlink, VR tools for interactive analysis of large data cubes, and specialized pipelines for solar feature extraction and radio observation preprocessing.

citations.claim: Image saturation has been an issue for several instruments in solar astronomy, mainly at EUV wavelengths; with the launch of AIA as part of SDO payload, image saturation became a big data issue involving around 10^$ frames per year since February 2010.
The paper introduces a novel desaturation method that recovers the signal in saturated regions of any AIA image by exploiting no other information but the one contained in the image itself.

The Open Science Data Federation (OSDF) integrates data origins and caches, and a use case with Big Bear Solar Observatory data provided standard, reliable data access worldwide, enabling pipelines to apply image processing techniques to all BBSO images.

Nanosatellites are limited by onboard memory and downlink speed; the proposed on-orbit system uses a lightweight CNN to classify and compress desirable image data for downlink prioritization, achieving about 100% classification accuracy on a star field dataset and compression ratios up to 5.43.

iDaVIE is a virtual reality software suite for interactive analysis of large 3D astronomical data cubes, integrated into workflows for verifying HI data cubes from MeerKAT, ASKAP, and APERTIF, addressing big-data challenges in modern astronomy.

SPACE-SUIT is an AI-based chromospheric feature extractor for the SUIT instrument on Aditya-L1, using a YOLO neural network to detect plages, sunspots, filaments, and off-limb structures, achieving precision of 0.788 and recall of 0.863.

RatanSunPy is an open-source Python package for processing RATAN-600 solar radio observations, providing calibration, quiet Sun normalization, and automatic detection of local sources and active regions for solar plasma studies.

standard.summary: The rapid advancement of mobile applications has generated significant demand for cross-platform compatibility, particularly between Android and iOS. Traditional approaches to mobile application translation rely on manual intervention or rule-based systems, which are labor-intensive and time-consuming. Recent machine-learning methods often lack contextual understanding and adaptability, leading to suboptimal translations. Large Language Models (LLMs) have been used to enhance code translation at method, class, and repository levels, but LLM-based application translation across platforms, such as Android-to-iOS migration, remains underexplored. A pilot study developed a chain-of-agents approach to translate Android applications to iOS, evaluating syntactic correctness, semantic accuracy, and functional completeness, and identifying key pitfalls and insights. Additionally, cross-platform development frameworks like React Native and Xamarin often fail to expose native APIs, requiring extra developer effort that partially negates the advantages of cross-platform development.

citations.claim: Traditional approaches to mobile application translation often rely on manual intervention or rule-based systems, which are labor-intensive and time-consuming.
LLM-based application translation across different platforms, such as migrating mobile applications between Android and iOS or adapting software across diverse frameworks, remains underexplored.
We developed a chain of agents that account for dependencies, specifications, program structure, and program control flow when translating applications from Android to iOS.

Most of the functionalities shared between native iOS and Android APIs are not available in React Native or Xamarin, and accessing the unavailable APIs requires additional effort by developers who need to know native APIs and write platform specific code.

balanced.summary: The documents highlight that the rapid growth of mobile applications has intensified the need for cross-platform compatibility, especially between Android and iOS. Traditional application translation relies heavily on manual or rule-based processes, which are labor-intensive and time-consuming [doc_1]. To address this, recent work leverages large language models (LLMs) for cross-platform translation and testing: an agentic LLM approach translates Android apps to iOS while accounting for dependencies and control flow [doc_1]; an LLM-based technique transfers UI tests across Android apps with high success [doc_3]; and an industrial framework generates acceptance test artifacts from requirements for Flutter-based cross-platform apps [doc_5]. Additional evidence shows that cross-platform development frameworks often lack full API support, requiring extra native-code effort [doc_2], and that automated test adaptation across similar apps can be approached as a search problem [doc_8]. Compatibility issues in mobile apps and games remain a critical challenge due to OS evolution and device fragmentation [doc_9].

citations.claim: Traditional approaches to mobile application translation often rely on manual intervention or rule-based systems, which are labor-intensive and time-consuming.
The study developed a chain of agents that account for dependencies, specifications, program structure, and program control flow when translating applications from Android to iOS.
LLMigrate leverages Large Language Models to transfer usage-based UI tests across mobile apps, achieving a 97.5% success rate and reducing manual effort by 91.1%.
AToMIC uses specialized LLMs to generate Gherkin scenarios, Page Objects, and executable UI test scripts directly from requirements, applied to BMW's MyBMW app in a cross-platform Flutter codebase.

Many screen-reader API functionalities shared between native iOS and Android are not available in React Native or Xamarin, and accessing unavailable APIs requires developers to write platform-specific code.
ADAPTDROID approaches test adaptation as a search problem and uses evolutionary testing to adapt GUI tests across similar Android apps.
The rapid evolution of mobile operating systems and device fragmentation make it challenging for developers to timely address compatibility issues across diverse device models.

standard.summary: Popular music streaming platforms provide users with a diverse network for content exploration through three affordances: organic, algorithmic, and editorial access modes. Although this offers great discovery potential, it also requires users to make daily adoption decisions about both platform affordances and the recommendations they receive. A longitudinal study of Deezer users found highly diverse behaviors and no blanket answer for adoption practices of recommendation features and recommendations.

citations.claim: Popular music streaming platforms offer users a diverse network of content exploration through a triad of affordances: organic, algorithmic and editorial access modes. Whilst offering great potential for discovery, such platform developments also pose the modern user with daily adoption decisions on two fronts: platform affordance adoption and the adoption of recommendations therein.
The resulting complex and quite heterogeneous picture demonstrates that there is no blanket answer for adoption practices of both recommendation features and recommendations.

balanced.summary: Music streaming platforms offer users a diverse network for content exploration through a triad of organic, algorithmic, and editorial access modes, but users exhibit highly diverse behavior in adopting these affordances and recommendations. The platform ecosystem also raises fairness concerns from artists, shapes hit songs differently across platforms, and can benefit from mechanisms such as song introductions and multinomial blending to support exploration and ranking. Different listener segments and longitudinal genre trajectories highlight the need for tailored recommender systems, while digital tools and streaming platforms may also drive homogenization in musical complexity.

citations.claim: Popular music streaming platforms offer users a diverse network of content exploration through a triad of affordances: organic, algorithmic and editorial access modes. Users exhibit very diverse behaviours in using and adopting the platform affordances, so there is no blanket answer for adoption practices.

Artists' perspective on fairness is underexplored; interviews identify aspects such as transparency, popularity bias, influencing users' listening behavior, and quotas for local music as relevant for fair music platforms.
Temporal analysis of musical compositions reveals a trend toward simplification across genres, suggesting that digital tools and streaming platforms foster new genres while driving homogenization.

TikTok and Spotify, situated in different governance and user contexts, show significant differences in major label, genre, and content features among hit songs, explained by distinct platformization practices.

Immersive and informative song introductions stimulate Taste-Broadening Serendipity, with transportation as the strongest predictor and cognitive elaboration as a weaker but easier-to-stimulate mechanism.
Metadata and AI-supported tools enable interactive and personalized audio-visual content production and consumption, though integration into existing infrastructures faces limitations.
Multinomial blending is a simple method for ranking items across different content types, useful for media streaming services with heterogeneous offerings like music, podcasts, and videos.

Beyond-mainstream music listeners comprise four subgroups differing in music preference and demographic characteristics, and the quality of music recommendations varies significantly across these subgroups.

Pathlet learning captures recurring patterns in genre trajectories, creating comprehensible trajectory embeddings that improve understanding of users' evolving musical preferences and diversity in recommender systems.

standard.summary: Fooling adversaries with traps such as honeytokens can slow cyber attacks and create strong indicators of compromise, but deception techniques are often poorly specified, and realistically measuring their effectiveness requires a well-exposed software system together with a production-ready implementation. Honeyquest addresses this challenge by translating 25 deception techniques into a high-level, machine-readable specification and using code-based questionnaires to measure enticingness without full implementation; experiments showed that the presence of cyber deception can reduce the risk that adversaries will find a true security risk by about 22% on average.

citations.claim: Fooling adversaries with traps such as honeytokens can slow down cyber attacks and create strong indicators of compromise. Unfortunately, cyber deception techniques are often poorly specified. Also, realistically measuring their effectiveness requires a well-exposed software system together with a production-ready implementation of these techniques.
Our open-source tool, Honeyquest, allows researchers to quickly evaluate the enticingness of deception techniques without implementing them.
We test the enticingness of 25 cyber deception techniques and 19 true security risks in an experiment with 47 humans.
We also show that the presence of cyber deception can significantly reduce the risk that adversaries will find a true security risk by about 22% on average.

balanced.summary: Cyber deception—using traps like honeytokens to fool adversaries—can slow attacks and create strong indicators of compromise, but techniques are often poorly specified and realistic effectiveness measurement normally requires fully exposed systems and production-ready implementations. Honeyquest addresses this by translating 25 deception techniques into machine-readable specifications and measuring their enticingness via code-based questionnaires, finding that deception reduced the risk of adversaries finding a true security risk by about 22%. Other works advance measurement and deployment: VelLMes evaluates LLM-based honeypots with human attackers and real internet traffic; MURHCAD provides a large empirical honeypot dataset for validating defenses; Koney operationalizes deception 'as code' on Kubernetes; application-layer techniques can be deployed without source-code access; decoy selection can be optimized using MITRE ATT&CK attack graphs; game-theoretic models (including non-zero-sum and Bayesian games) inform optimal honeypot placement; Siren combines deception with machine learning and adaptive analysis; and AI deception itself is framed as a sociotechnical risk with emergence and treatment components. Together, these sources show both the promise of deception and the need for clearer specification, realistic evaluation, and operationalizable deployment.

citations.claim: Cyber deception techniques are often poorly specified, and realistically measuring their effectiveness requires a well-exposed software system together with a production-ready implementation; Honeyquest translated 25 techniques into machine-readable specifications and found that deception reduced the risk of adversaries finding a true security risk by about 22% on average.

MURHCAD is a high-resolution honeypot dataset containing 132,425 attack events from Cowrie, Dionaea, and SentryPeer across four regions over 72 hours, enabling reproducible, cloud-scale investigations of global cyberattack behaviors for anomaly detection, threat intelligence, and defensive policy design.

VelLMes is an AI-based deception framework that simulates multiple protocols including SSH Linux shell, MySQL, POP3, and HTTP; evaluation with 89 human attackers showed about 30% believed they were interacting with a real system when assigned an LLM-based honeypot, and internet-deployed instances responded correctly to most unstructured commands.

Application-layer cyber deception can be deployed at application runtime without full control over the software development lifecycle; the work reviews 19 technical methods and identifies novel techniques beyond honeypots and reverse proxies that have received little research interest despite their promise.

A proactive decoy selection scheme using MITRE ATT&CK-based attack graphs and graph partitioning minimizes the number of decoys needed to detect techniques in attack paths, achieving the highest interception rate with the lowest amount of decoys compared to benchmarks.

Siren integrates deception, machine learning, and proactive threat analysis through a link monitoring proxy, a dynamic machine learning model for link analysis, and a honeypot with simulated user interactions and probabilistic encryption, enabling the system to actively engage and learn from adversaries.

AI deception is defined using signaling theory, organized as a deception cycle with deception emergence and treatment, and analyzed in terms of capability preconditions, contextual triggers, detection methods, and mitigation strategies spanning technical, community, and governance efforts.

A non-zero-sum game model derives Nash equilibria for cyber attacker-defender interactions, showing that high-probability low-cost exploits like Phishing and Social Engineering are more likely to be used by attackers and that increasing the number of network nodes dilutes attacker effort, improving defender payoff.

Koney introduces deception policy documents to describe deception technology 'as code' and uses a Kubernetes operator with service meshes and eBPF to set up, rotate, monitor, and remove traps in containerized applications without source-code access, focusing on maintainability, scalability, and simplicity.

In Blockchain-based IoT systems, an AI-powered model with an Intrusion Detection System and smart contracts enables dynamic honeypot deployment, transforming regular nodes into decoys in response to suspicious activities; Bayesian game analysis supports strategic decision-making and adaptive honeypot placement.
