standard.summary: Speech emotion recognition (SER) plays a pivotal role in human-computer interaction, enabling systems to decipher emotional states from speech and physiological signals, with applications in empathetic conversational agents, user experience evaluation, and psychological assessment. Recent advances include high-resolution neural networks achieving state-of-the-art accuracy (EmoHRNet), focal-loss residual CNNs for robust feature learning, and audio language models with contextual perception and chain-of-thought reasoning. Physiological approaches using EEG also show promise for emotion classification. Speech analysis has been validated as an objective proxy for user experience, addressing biases in self-report questionnaires. However, challenges persist: real-time emotion recognition is limited by accuracy, emotional transition speeds, personality effects, and voice tone modulation; models struggle with cross-subject/cross-session generalization and dataset shift; and real-world conditions such as distance, shouting, and varied environments degrade performance. These findings highlight both progress and remaining obstacles in applying SER to psychological and interactive contexts.

citations.claim: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is pivotal for enhancing human-machine interactions.
Integrating neural and physiological signals into conversational agents enables real-time emotion recognition and empathetic responses.
Acoustic and prosodic speech features can differentiate positive and neutral user experience, offering an objective and bias-resistant complement to self-report questionnaires.
EmoHRNet achieves state-of-the-art SER accuracy, e.g., 92.45% on RAVDESS, 80.06% on IEMOCAP, and 92.77% on EMOVO.
A Residual CNN trained with Focal Loss uses spectrogram and MFCC features to recognize emotion in speech, focusing on hard examples.
An EEG-based Random Forest model classified happiness, relaxation, and sadness with up to 97.21% accuracy for happiness.
Large audio language models suffer from hallucinations in SER; C2SER uses contextual perception and chain-of-thought to improve stability.
Challenges for real-time emotion recognition include recognition accuracy, emotional transition speeds, individual personality effects, and voice tone modulation limitations.
Non-stationarity of EEG signals leads to dataset shift, and transfer learning methods are key for improving cross-subject and cross-session generalization in EEG-based emotion recognition.
The BERSt dataset shows that ASR and SER degrade with increased distance, shout level, and varied acoustic environments, indicating real-world robustness remains challenging.

balanced.summary: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is a key enabler in human-computer interaction (HCI), supporting psychological assessment by decoding emotional states from voice and related signals. Recent advances include high-accuracy models such as EmoHRNet, which achieves strong results on benchmark SER datasets, and C2SER, which reduces hallucinations in audio language models using contextual perception and chain-of-thought reasoning. Other innovations apply speech feature analysis to evaluate user experience and user satisfaction in voice interfaces, employ EEG signals for emotion classification, and use large language models for text-based emotion detection. Despite this progress, multiple challenges remain: real-time emotion recognition struggles with accuracy, emotional transition speeds, individual personality differences, and voice tone modulation; real-world SER and ASR degrade with shouted, distanced, or emotionally varied speech; audio language models still hallucinate; EEG-based emotion recognition suffers from cross-subject/cross-session dataset shift; and traditional questionnaire-based UX evaluation remains subjective, suggesting speech as a potential objective alternative.

citations.claim: Integrating neural and physiological signals into empathetic conversational agents enables real-time emotion recognition, but challenges include recognition accuracy, emotional transition speeds, individual personality effects, and voice tone modulation limitations.
EmoHRNet, a High-Resolution Network adapted for SER, achieves accuracies of 92.45% on RAVDESS, 80.06% on IEMOCAP, and 92.77% on EMOVO, setting a new benchmark in speech emotion recognition.

Speech-derived audio features such as temporal, spectral, and linguistic markers correlate with self-reported satisfaction and experience in voice assistants, and a machine learning model trained on these features can classify UX levels with promising accuracy.

A Random Forest model using EEG signals from a brain-computer interface achieved 97.21% accuracy for happiness, 76% for relaxation, and 76% for sadness, and was used to build a real-time emotion prediction algorithm.

The BERSt dataset, containing shouted and distanced speech from 98 actors, demonstrates that ASR degrades with increased distance and shout level, showing varied performance depending on intended emotion, and remains challenging for both ASR and SER tasks.

Large-scale audio language models often suffer from hallucinations in SER, but the proposed C2SER, using Whisper and Emotion2Vec-S encoders with chain-of-thought and self-distillation, outperforms existing popular ALMs in stability and accuracy.

Acoustic and prosodic speech features such as RMS, zero-crossing rate, jitter, and shimmer significantly differentiate positive versus neutral UX, highlighting speech analysis as an objective and bias-resistant tool for HCI evaluation.

A Residual Convolutional Neural Network trained with Focal Loss on spectrogram and MFCC features focuses training on hard examples, improving speech emotion recognition over plain text-based features.

A systematic review of EEG-based emotion recognition identifies non-stationarity of EEG signals and dataset shift as critical issues, with transfer learning methods performing better than other approaches for cross-subject and cross-session generalization.

Large language models can identify emotions in text by drawing upon psychology-based emotion models, contributing to more responsive and sensitive human-computer interaction, though they were evaluated against a state-of-the-art model on the GoEmotions dataset.

standard.summary: A multi-arm robotic platform for scientific exploration is positioned against a backdrop of many surgical multi-arm platforms; however, few groups have used such platforms for scientific exploration. Possible scientific applications include studying mechanisms of intractable diseases using organoids, which requires preparing a cranial window by removing an 8 mm skull patch in mice. The first prototype, its digital twins, and teleoperated validation experiments were presented, including peg transfer, gauze cutting, mock egg experiments, and the world's first four-hand teleoperated drilling for a cranial window. The digital twins and control software are freely available for noncommercial use.

citations.claim: There are a large number of robotic platforms with two or more arms targeting surgical applications. Despite that, very few groups have employed such platforms for scientific exploration. Possible applications of a multi-arm platform in scientific exploration involve the study of the mechanisms of intractable diseases by using organoids, i.e., miniature human organs. The study of organoids requires the preparation of a cranial window, which is done by carefully removing an 8 mm patch of the skull of a mouse.

The experiments showcase the dexterity of the platform by performing peg transfer, gauze cutting, mock experiments using eggs, and the world's first four-hand teleoperated drilling for a cranial window. The digital twins and related control software are freely available for noncommercial use.

balanced.summary: The observation in the query is directly supported by doc_1: many multi-arm robotic platforms target surgical applications, yet few groups have used such platforms for scientific exploration. Doc_1 presents a multi-arm AI-robot science platform whose possible scientific applications include studying mechanisms of intractable diseases using organoids; its validation experiments involved teleoperated dexterity tests and the first four-hand teleoperated cranial-window drilling, an 8-mm skull-patch removal required for organoid studies. A dual-arm robotic setup was used to automate tissue traction with miniature force-sensing forceps and validate resections on ex vivo tissues, demonstrating a surgical application of multi-arm robotics.

standard.summary: DP-coloring was introduced by Dvořák and Postle as a generalization of list coloring and signed coloring; the paper also introduces strictly f-degenerate transversal as a further generalization of DP-coloring and L-forested-coloring. It presents structural results on planar and toroidal graphs with forbidden configurations and uses them to establish sufficient conditions for strictly f-degenerate transversal, yielding results such as: every toroidal graph without certain configurations is DP-4-colorable and has list vertex arboricity at most 2; every toroidal graph without 4-cycles is DP-4-colorable and has list vertex arboricity at most 2; and every planar graph without certain configurations is DP-4-colorable and has list vertex arboricity at most 2.

citations.claim: DP-coloring was introduced by Dvořák and Postle as a generalization of list coloring and signed coloring; a new coloring, strictly f-degenerate transversal, is a further generalization of DP-coloring and L-forested-coloring. The paper presents structural results on planar and toroidal graphs with forbidden configurations and establishes sufficient conditions for the existence of strictly f-degenerate transversal, leading to DP-4-colorability and list vertex arboricity at most 2 for certain toroidal and planar graphs.

balanced.summary: The paper introduces and studies a new coloring called strictly f-degenerate transversal, which generalizes both DP-coloring and L-forested-coloring. DP-coloring was originally introduced by Dvořák and Postle as a generalization of list coloring and signed coloring. The paper presents structural results on planar and toroidal graphs with forbidden configurations and establishes sufficient conditions for the existence of strictly f-degenerate transversals. As consequences, it proves that every toroidal graph without certain configurations or without 4-cycles is DP-4-colorable and has list vertex arboricity at most 2, and similarly for planar graphs without certain configurations. These results improve earlier bounds on DP-4-coloring and list vertex arboricity.

standard.summary: Analyzing user behavior from usability evaluation is challenging and time-consuming, especially as the number of participants and the scale and complexity of the evaluation grows. To address this, uxSense is proposed as a visual analytics system that uses machine learning methods (including pattern recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, and machine learning) to extract user behavior from audio and video recordings as parallel time-stamped data streams, visualized as parallel timelines for searching, filtering, and annotating data.

citations.claim: Analyzing user behavior from usability evaluation can be a challenging and time-consuming task, especially as the number of participants and the scale and complexity of the evaluation grows. uxSense is a visual analytics system using machine learning methods to extract user behavior from audio and video recordings as parallel time-stamped data streams, visualized as parallel timelines in a web-based front-end.

balanced.summary: Analyzing user behavior from usability evaluation is challenging and time-consuming, especially as participant numbers and the scale/complexity of the evaluation grow. To address this, uxSense is proposed: a visual analytics system that uses machine learning, pattern recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, and ML to extract features such as user sentiment, actions, posture, and spoken words from audio/video recordings as parallel time-stamped data streams, visualized as parallel timelines for searching, filtering, and annotating. Other recent approaches also target usability evaluation challenges: LLMs like GPT-4o can assist heuristic evaluation but with limitations (only 21.2% overlap with human experts and false positives), and LLM-agent frameworks such as UXAgent allow automatic generation of simulated users to test web designs before human studies. Empirical studies, such as a family of experiments with 367 subjects, continue to validate usability mechanisms' impact on efficiency, effectiveness, and satisfaction.

A family of three experiments with 367 subjects found that Abort Operation and Preferences usability mechanisms improve system usability with respect to efficiency, effectiveness, and user satisfaction.

standard.summary: Algorithms operating on real numbers are typically implemented as floating-point computations in practice, but floating-point operations introduce roundoff errors that can degrade the accuracy of the result. To address this, a functional programming language called Λ_num is proposed, featuring a type system that can express quantitative bounds on roundoff error. The type system combines sensitivity analysis via a linear typing discipline with a graded monad to track roundoff error accumulation, and its soundness is proved by relating denotational semantics to exact and floating-point operational semantics. It also instantiates error metrics from numerical analysis and models IEEE 754 rounding behaviors, with a prototype implementation that infers competitive error bounds while often running faster.

citations.claim: Algorithms operating on real numbers are implemented as floating-point computations in practice, but floating-point operations introduce roundoff errors that can degrade the accuracy of the result. We propose Λ_num, a functional programming language with a type system that can express quantitative bounds on roundoff error.

Our type system combines a sensitivity analysis, enforced through a linear typing discipline, with a novel graded monad to track the accumulation of roundoff errors. We prove that our type system is sound by relating the denotational semantics of our language to the exact and floating-point operational semantics.

To demonstrate our system, we instantiate Λ_num with error metrics proposed in the numerical analysis literature and we show how to incorporate rounding operations that faithfully model aspects of the IEEE 754 floating-point standard.

To show that Λ_num can be a useful tool for automated error analysis, we develop a prototype implementation for Λ_num that infers error bounds that are competitive with existing tools, while often running significantly faster.

balanced.summary: Floating-point implementations of real-number algorithms are common in practice, but each floating-point operation can introduce roundoff errors that degrade the accuracy of the result. To address this, the paper proposes Λnum, a functional programming language with a type system that expresses quantitative bounds on roundoff error: it combines a sensitivity analysis enforced via a linear typing discipline with a novel graded monad to track the accumulation of roundoff errors, and it proves soundness by relating the language's denotational semantics to exact and floating-point operational semantics. A prototype implementation infers error bounds competitive with existing tools. Broader literature reinforces the importance of this problem: attainable accuracy depends on the floating-point number system, arbitrary precision and interval arithmetic can mitigate errors, and formal error models such as relative precision support certified bounds.

citations.claim: Algorithms operating on real numbers are implemented as floating-point computations in practice, but floating-point operations introduce roundoff errors that can degrade the accuracy of the result.

Λnum is a functional programming language with a type system that can express quantitative bounds on roundoff error, combining a sensitivity analysis enforced through a linear typing discipline with a novel graded monad to track the accumulation of roundoff errors.

The type system's soundness is proven by relating the denotational semantics of the language to exact and floating-point operational semantics, and a prototype implementation infers error bounds that are competitive with existing tools.
Different choices of floating-point number systems, including base/radix and normalized versus unnormalized representation, affect the attainable numerical accuracy.
Arbitrary precision numbers and calculations can minimize truncation and rounding errors, which is important when computations involve very small and very large numbers simultaneously.
Relative precision is a rounding error model that forms a true metric, propagates error bounds through computations, and slightly overapproximates the standard rounding error model.
Verifying floating-point computations is tricky because semantics may change with factors beyond source code, such as choices made by compilers.

Arb is an arbitrary-precision interval arithmetic library using midpoint-radius representation that supports efficient error bounds for real and complex numbers, polynomials, power series, and special functions.

standard.summary: The described work is motivated by computing sample covariance matrices and transforming a collection of vectors to a sparse basis; it presents a simple randomized algorithm that approximates the product of two n-by-n real matrices A and B using 2-wise independent hash functions and an FFT-based polynomial compression, yielding an unbiased estimator with variance bounded by ||AB||_F^2 / b in time ~O(n^2 + n b).

standard.summary: The paper introduces fully adaptive and semi-adaptive frequency sweep algorithms for electromagnetic simulation of multiport systems, built on a Loewner matrix-based state model. The proposed algorithms use two Loewner matrix models—with either different or the same orders and a small frequency perturbation—to guide adaptive frequency selection. In each iteration, the error between the two models is computed, and the next frequency points are chosen to minimize the maximum error; the algorithm stops when the model error reaches the specified tolerance relative to the simulation result. The fully adaptive variant starts from the minimum and maximum frequencies, while the semi-adaptive variant determines the initial number of frequency points based on the electrical size of the structure. Compared with the Stoer-Bulirsch algorithm and Pradovera's minimal sampling algorithm, the proposed methods offer better speed, accuracy, and use fewer frequency samples, showing strong consistency with full-wave simulation data.

citations.claim: The paper employs a fully adaptive and semi-adaptive frequency sweep algorithm using the Loewner matrix-based state model for electromagnetic simulation.
The proposed algorithms use two Loewner matrix models with different or the same orders with small frequency perturbation for adaptive frequency selection.
The error between the two models is calculated in each iteration, and the next frequency points are selected to minimize maximum error.

In the fully adaptive frequency sweep algorithm, the method starts with the minimum and maximum frequency of simulation; in the semi-adaptive algorithm, the initial number of frequency points is determined based on the electrical size of the structure.

The proposed algorithms were compared with the Stoer-Bulirsch algorithm and Pradovera's minimal sampling algorithm, showing better speed, accuracy, and minimum number of frequency samples, with remarkable consistency to full-wave simulation data.

balanced.summary: The paper described in [doc_1] employs fully-adaptive and semi-adaptive frequency sweep algorithms for electromagnetic simulation of multiport systems, using a Loewner matrix-based state model. The algorithms compare two Loewner models with different or same orders under small frequency perturbation to adaptively select frequency points, minimizing the maximum error and terminating once the error is within tolerance; the semi-adaptive variant determines the initial number of frequency points from the structure's electrical size. The methods are reported to outperform the Stoer-Bulirsch algorithm and Pradovera's minimal sampling in speed, accuracy, and minimum number of frequency samples. Related work in [doc_2] also applies adaptive error estimates within the Loewner framework to reduce the number of full-wave simulations for multiport array antennas.

citations.claim: This paper employs a fully adaptive and semi-adaptive frequency sweep algorithm using the Loewner matrix-based state model for the electromagnetic simulation.
The proposed algorithms use two Loewner matrix models with different or the same orders with small frequency perturbation for adaptive frequency selection.

The proposed algorithms have been compared with the Stoer-Bulirsch algorithm and Pradovera's minimal sampling algorithm for electromagnetic simulation, showing better performance in speed, accuracy, and the requirement of the minimum number of frequency samples.

Data-driven model order reduction algorithms, such as the Loewner framework and vector fitting, can be integrated with adaptive error estimates in an iterative algorithm to reduce the number of full-wave simulations required to accurately capture the requested frequency behavior of multiport array antennas.

Two novel adaptive methods exploit a block matrix function which is a key part of the Loewner framework; the first leverages an inherent matrix parameter freedom to identify frequency points with large errors, whereas the second utilizes the condition number of the block matrix function.

standard.summary: Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are efficient and widely used solvers for large sparse linear systems arising from PDE discretizations, with potential near-linear complexity. However, they have severe limitations: they are designed primarily for symmetric positive definite (SPD) problems and can struggle with anisotropic diffusion, non-symmetric or indefinite systems, saddle-point structures, and tightly coupled multiphysics problems, often requiring problem-specific adaptations or failing when standard assumptions are violated.

citations.claim: AMG is a popular and effective iterative method for large sparse linear systems from PDE discretization, but while designed for SPD matrices, certain SPD problems such as anisotropic diffusion are not adequately addressed, and non-SPD problems pose an even greater challenge.

When a phase disappears in the complementarity approach for two-phase flow with phase transitions, the linear system has a saddle point structure and becomes indefinite, so current algebraic multigrid algorithms cannot be applied directly.

For non-symmetric matrices, theoretical convergence results for AMG have been provided only recently, with the M-matrix property being sufficient for convergence; problems can occur when this property is violated.

Current state-of-the-art 'black-box' solvers such as algebraic multigrid are ineffective for multiphase poromechanics because they cannot effectively capture the strong coupling between the mechanics and the flow sub-problems.

Iterative solvers based on algebraic multigrid preconditioners can reach up to linear complexity for sufficiently regular problems but do not always converge and require more knowledge from the user for an efficient setup.

balanced.summary: Algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are efficient and widely used iterative solvers for large sparse linear systems arising from PDE discretizations, with the potential for near-linear O(n) complexity and established convergence theory for symmetric positive definite (SPD) problems. However, AMG has severe limitations for several practically important problem classes: non-symmetric and indefinite systems, saddle-point problems arising e.g. in multiphase flow with phase transitions, strongly anisotropic diffusion, and tightly coupled multiphysics problems such as multiphase poromechanics. In such cases standard AMG may not converge, cannot be applied directly, or is ineffective as a black-box solver. Research addresses these limitations with specialized variants such as root-node AMG, energy-minimization prolongation, adaptive AMG, multigrid reduction frameworks, and neural-network-based parameter prediction.

citations.claim: AMG is used for solving large scale systems of equations such as those from discretization of PDEs; a unified framework derives optimal coarse spaces and proves uniform convergence for two-level AMG with respect to problem size, coefficient variation, and anisotropy.
AMG is one of the most widely used solution techniques for linear systems arising from discretized PDEs, with the potential to solve them in almost linear time (O(n) complexity).

AMG is designed for SPD matrices, but certain SPD problems such as anisotropic diffusion are not adequately addressed, and non-SPD problems pose an even greater challenge; in practice AMG is often not considered as a solver for such problems.

In two-phase flow with phase transitions using a complementarity formulation, when a phase disappears the linear system becomes a saddle-point problem and indefinite, so current AMG algorithms cannot be applied directly.

For SPD matrices convergence theory is established, but for non-symmetric matrices convergence results are recent; a sufficient condition is that the matrix be an M-matrix, and problems can occur when this property is violated.

Current state-of-the-art black-box solvers such as AMG are ineffective for multiphase poromechanics because they cannot effectively capture the strong coupling between mechanics and the flow sub-problems.
AMG-based iterative solvers can reach up to linear complexity for sufficiently regular problems but do not always converge and require more user knowledge for an efficient setup.
Artificial neural networks can be used to predict the strong connection parameter in AMG construction to maximize the convergence factor of the AMG scheme.

standard.summary: The paper studies spectrum allocation mechanisms in hierarchical multi-layer markets, which are expected to proliferate in the near future following current spectrum policy reform proposals. The setting involves a state agency selling spectrum channels to Primary Operators (POs), who then resell them to Secondary Operators (SOs) through auctions. The analysis shows these hierarchical markets fail to achieve socially efficient spectrum allocation because of lack of coordination across layers and POs' selfish revenue-maximizing behavior. To address this, the paper proposes an incentive mechanism that aligns POs' strategies with the agency's objective, improving social welfare via a pricing-based regulatory scheme that includes a novel auction balancing PO revenue and SO welfare.

citations.claim: The paper studies spectrum allocation mechanisms in hierarchical multi-layer markets expected to proliferate in the near future based on current spectrum policy reform proposals, in a setting where a state agency sells spectrum channels to Primary Operators (POs) who resell them to Secondary Operators (SOs) through auctions.

Hierarchical markets do not result in socially efficient spectrum allocation due to lack of coordination among entities in different layers and the selfish revenue-maximizing strategy of POs, so the paper proposes an incentive mechanism aligning POs with the agency's objective to improve social welfare.

The proposed incentive mechanism is a pricing-based scheme for hierarchical market regulation, with a novel auction scheme that lets POs allocate spectrum by balancing derived revenue and the welfare of the SOs.

standard.summary: Automated Speaking Assessment (ASA) is crucial for evaluating second-language (L2) learners' proficiency, but ASA models often suffer from class imbalance, which leads to biased predictions. To mitigate this, a Balancing Logit Variation (BLV) loss is introduced that perturbs model predictions to improve feature representation for minority classes without altering the dataset, and evaluations on the ICNALE benchmark demonstrate enhanced classification accuracy and fairness, making automated speech evaluation more robust for diverse learners.

citations.claim: Automated Speaking Assessment (ASA) plays a crucial role in evaluating second-language (L2) learners proficiency. However, ASA models often suffer from class imbalance, leading to biased predictions.

To address this, we introduce a novel objective for training ASA models, dubbed the Balancing Logit Variation (BLV) loss, which perturbs model predictions to improve feature representation for minority classes without modifying the dataset.

balanced.summary: Automated Speaking Assessment (ASA) is crucial for evaluating L2 learners' proficiency, but ASA models often suffer from class imbalance, causing biased predictions; the Balancing Logit Variation (BLV) loss addresses this by perturbing predictions to improve feature representation for minority classes without modifying the dataset, yielding better accuracy and fairness on the ICNALE benchmark. Related automated assessment research tackles similar challenges: ASR-based oral reading assessment and reading tutors improve with language-model design and careful evaluation (docs 2, 6); wav2vec2/Whisper frameworks enable scalable classroom speech analysis and acceptable ASR performance for non-native child speech (docs 7, 10); transfer learning improves speech quality prediction under limited data (doc 3); feature-selected NLP models accurately classify L2 proficiency levels (doc 4); grammatical microsystems predict L2 writing proficiency (doc 8); LLM-based grading frameworks reduce uncertainty and bias in automated grading (doc 5); and speech-integrated LLMs can exhibit demographic biases that require multi-method evaluation (doc 9).

citations.claim: Automated Speaking Assessment (ASA) plays a crucial role in evaluating second-language learners' proficiency, but ASA models suffer from class imbalance, leading to biased predictions; the Balancing Logit Variation (BLV) loss perturbs model predictions to improve feature representation for minority classes without modifying the dataset, significantly enhancing classification accuracy and fairness on the ICNALE benchmark.

Automatic assessment of oral reading accuracy using ASR holds potential for reading diagnostics; including reading errors in the language model improves assessment performance, as shown by a Dutch system reaching substantial agreement with human evaluations (MCC = .63).

Non-intrusive speech quality prediction with only 100 labeled utterances can be improved through two-stage transfer learning with wav2vec 2.0; it achieved the best BAK prediction (LCC=0.867) and improved SIG prediction from 0.207 to 0.516 when adding artificially degraded data.

NLP classification of Estonian learner texts can predict CEFR levels with around 0.9 accuracy using pre-selected lexical, morphological, surface, and error features, supporting explainable and generalizable language proficiency assessment.

The Grade Guard framework for automated short answer grading introduces confidence-aware loss and an indecisiveness score to reduce LLM grading inaccuracies, outperforming traditional methods by up to 23.64% RMSE across various LLMs.

ASR-based reading tutor applications can provide feedback to first-graders, but ASR classification accuracy varies for different reading tasks and word types, and isolated words are difficult to classify in the current configuration.

The WSW2.0 framework integrates wav2vec2-based speaker classification and Whisper transcription to analyze preschool classroom speech, achieving weighted F1 of .845 for speaker classification and moderate-to-high transcription quality, and scaling to over 1,592 hours of audio.
Seven grammatical microsystems operationalized via supervised learning are significant predictors of L2 writing proficiency and can be used in CALL systems for proficiency assessment.

Speech-integrated large language models can amplify biases in training data; gender bias levels are language-dependent and vary with evaluation methods, emphasizing the need for multiple bias assessment approaches.

Recent pre-trained ASR transformer models (Wav2Vec2.0 and Whisper) achieve acceptable performance on native and non-native Dutch child speech, allowing detailed phoneme pronunciation feedback for language learning voicebots.

standard.summary: Viscoelastic two-phase flows arise in many industrial and natural processes, making the development of accurate and efficient numerical simulation software a highly relevant and challenging research task. To address this, doc_1 presents a geometrical unstructured Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) method for two-phase flows with a viscoelastic liquid phase, using generic rate-type constitutive equations and a one-field description derived from conditional volume averaging. The method extends the plicRDF-isoAdvector VOF solver within the DeboRheo framework, applies piecewise-linear interface reconstruction on general unstructured meshes to discretize viscoelastic stresses across the interface, and supports flexible combinations of rheological models with stabilization techniques for the high Weissenberg number problem.

citations.claim: Viscoelastic two-phase flows arise in various industrial and natural processes, and developing accurate and efficient software for their detailed numerical simulation is a highly relevant and challenging research task.

A geometrical unstructured un-split VOF method is presented for viscoelastic two-phase flows, employing piecewise-linear interface reconstruction on unstructured meshes and the DeboRheo framework to handle viscoelastic stresses and the high Weissenberg number problem.

balanced.summary: Viscoelastic two-phase flows occur in many industrial and natural settings, making the development of accurate and efficient numerical simulation software a highly relevant and challenging research task (doc_1). The provided documents present a diverse set of numerical methods and analyses that address this challenge from different angles: unstructured geometric VOF with viscoelastic stress modeling (doc_1), space-time adaptive simulation of shear-thinning mold filling (doc_2), Riemann solvers for compressible two-phase systems (doc_3), open-boundary phase-field algorithms (doc_4), DPG-based validation of viscoelastic material models (doc_5), thermodynamically extended symplectic schemes for viscoelastic solids (doc_6), a priori error estimates for transient flow problems (doc_7), non-oscillatory energy-splitting for multi-fluid flows (doc_8), velocity and energy relaxation models for two-phase flows (doc_9), and Eulerian finite-volume interface methods for multi-material flows (doc_10). Collectively, these works underscore the breadth of numerical techniques required for robust, accurate simulation of viscoelastic and multiphase flow phenomena.

citations.claim: Viscoelastic two-phase flows arise in various industrial and natural processes, and developing accurate and efficient software for their detailed numerical simulation is a highly relevant and challenging research task; the paper presents a geometrical unstructured VOF method for such flows with rate-type constitutive equations.

Simulation of highly viscous non-isothermal two-phase flow during mold filling uses the Carreau-WLF shear-thinning model and 4D simplex space-time meshes with local temporal refinement for improved accuracy and efficiency.

A new Riemann solver with internal reconstruction (RSIR) is built to address complex compressible two-phase flow models, handling stationary volume fraction discontinuities, transport waves, shocks and expansion waves accurately.

New open boundary conditions and a rotational pressure-correction algorithm for two-phase outflow simulations yield linear systems with constant, time-independent coefficient matrices despite variable density and viscosity.

A discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin method for time-harmonic linear viscoelasticity, with an arbitrary-p a posteriori error estimator, successfully validates DMA calibration models of epoxy and silicone resins to within 5%.

Thermodynamically extended symplectic schemes for 1D viscoelastic wave propagation coupled with heat conduction via thermal expansion demonstrate long-term reliability and use thermodynamics-based quantities to supervise solution quality.
A priori error estimates in the discrete-time setting for transient problems with Dirichlet boundary conditions are derived, useful for determining time step size and space discretization size.

A non-oscillatory energy-splitting conservative algorithm for compressible multi-fluid flows suppresses nonphysical oscillations around material interfaces, as shown in shock-interface and shock-bubble interaction problems.

Analytical investigation of velocity and energy relaxation in two-phase flows shows that as relaxation time tends to zero, a simplified two-phase model is obtained, suitable for violent aerated flows.

The Enhanced-NIP method improves the former FVCF-NIP Eulerian finite volume method for compressible multi-material flows by curing an inconsistency in interface reconstruction, improving shape conservation and stability.

standard.summary: Numerical calculations of 2-D steady incompressible driven cavity flow are presented using the Navier-Stokes equations in streamfunction-vorticity formulation, solved numerically on a fine uniform 601x601 grid. Solutions were obtained for Reynolds numbers below 21,000 with maximum absolute residuals less than 10^-10, and detailed results were compared with benchmark solutions in the literature.

citations.claim: Numerical calculations of the 2-D steady incompressible driven cavity flow are presented, with the Navier-Stokes equations in streamfunction and vorticity formulation solved numerically using a fine uniform grid mesh of 601x601.

The steady driven cavity solutions are computed for Re<21,000 with a maximum absolute residuals of the governing equations that were less than 10^-10, and detailed results are presented with comparisons to benchmark solutions.

balanced.summary: The numerical calculations of steady incompressible driven cavity flow using the streamfunction-vorticity formulation on a fine uniform grid are presented in doc_1, which solves the 2-D steady incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on a 601x601 grid for Reynolds numbers up to 21,000 with residuals below 10^-10 and reports new vortical structures. A related fourth-order compact formulation is described in doc_2, also solved on a 601x601 grid up to Re=20,000. Doc_3 provides context on the physical vs. numerical 2-D nature of driven cavity flow. Additional numerical approaches include a two-level finite element method for the stream function formulation in doc_4 and an Eulerian vortex method applied to cavity flow in doc_6.

citations.claim: Numerical calculations of the 2-D steady incompressible driven cavity flow are presented, solving the Navier-Stokes equations in streamfunction and vorticity formulation numerically using a fine uniform grid mesh of 601x601 for Re<21,000 with maximum absolute residuals less than 10^-10.

A fourth order compact formulation for the steady 2-D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations is solved with an efficient numerical method using a fine grid mesh of 601x601, achieving fourth order spatial accuracy up to Reynolds number 20,000.

The driven cavity flow is discussed, noting that above moderate Reynolds numbers physically the flow is not two-dimensional, although numerical solutions for 2-D driven cavity flow at high Reynolds numbers exist.

A two-level finite element method is implemented for the stream function formulation of the Navier-Stokes equations, with the driven cavity problem used as a test case and stream function contours showing main flow features.

An Eulerian vortex method based on flow maps is demonstrated for incompressible fluid simulations, including cavity flow and the formation of complex vortical structures due to solid-fluid interactions.

standard.summary: In the past decade, rising wind power penetration has focused worldwide attention on the variable and stochastic nature of wind generation, which makes electric-system dispatch and planning more complex. Because wind is intermittent and uncertain, traditional unit commitment and dispatch methods must be modified to maintain reliability, and forecasting is needed to support grid dispatch. The variability of wind also increases risks of overloads and cascading events, and it introduces uncertainty into optimal power flow. At the planning level, high renewables integration requires transmission infrastructure expansion or creative use of existing assets, and the growth of distributed renewable generation makes operation and planning computationally harder.

citations.claim: Increasing wind penetration and the stochastic nature of wind force an alteration of traditional methods for solving day-ahead and look-ahead unit commitment and dispatch.
Variability of wind generation increases the risk of unexpected overloads and cascading events.
Uncontrollable wind generation increases the risk of random component failures, altering traditional unit commitment and dispatch.
Energy forecasting (including wind) provides a reference for subsequent tasks such as power grid dispatch, bringing economic benefits.
Wind-farm caused fluctuations and inherent uncertainties require probabilistic chance-constrained optimal power flow that is computationally tractable.

High renewables integration and inflected variabilities in power flows demand expansion of transmission infrastructure, and require creative use of existing grid via technologies such as FACTS devices.
The rise of distributed renewable generation creates computational challenges for operation and planning in networks with many buses and decentral generators.
Integration of large shares of wind power benefits from transmission network expansion; Dynamic Line Rating can improve integration of renewables while reducing grid congestion.
Future power systems without fuel will require new system-level models and control methods for semiconductor-based energy-conversion interfaces.

balanced.summary: Over the past decade, wind energy has gained worldwide attention because of its indirectness and volatility; as wind power penetration has increased, it has made the dispatching and planning of electric power systems more difficult and complex. The stochastic nature of wind challenges traditional unit commitment and dispatch methods, requiring new formulations for security-constrained scheduling, forecasting, and grid planning. Forecasting is essential because it supports grid dispatch and must account for external factors and downstream dispatch costs. Wind-induced fluctuations further complicate optimal power flow and contingency management. Growing renewables penetration also drives the need for transmission expansion, reactive power support, and faster computational tools for operation and planning, while long-term planning must consider climate-change impacts on wind resource reliability.

citations.claim: As renewable wind energy penetration rates continue to increase, one of the major challenges facing grid operators is the question of how to control transmission grids in a reliable and a cost-efficient manner; the stochastic nature of wind forces an alteration of traditional methods for solving day-ahead and look-ahead unit commitment and dispatch.

The stochastic nature of wind forces an alteration of traditional methods for solving day-ahead and look-ahead unit commitment and dispatch, and uncontrollable wind generation increases the risk of random component failures.

Energy (load, wind, photovoltaic) forecasting is significant in the power industry as it can provide a reference for subsequent tasks such as power grid dispatch, thus bringing huge economic benefits; energy forecasting aims to minimize the cost of subsequent tasks such as power grid dispatch, rather than simply pursuing prediction accuracy.

One of the most common control decisions faced by power system operators is the question of how to dispatch generation to meet demand for power, a complex optimization problem that includes many nonlinear, nonconvex constraints as well as inherent uncertainties about future demand and available generation; the paper models wind-farm caused fluctuations.

Decentralized electricity markets and more integration of renewables demand expansion of the existing transmission infrastructure to accommodate inflected variabilities in power flows, and high renewables integration requires additional reactive power support, forcing transmission system operators to utilize the existing grid creatively.

The integration of large shares of wind and solar power into the power system benefits from transmission network expansion, but construction of new power lines requires long planning phases and is often delayed; Dynamic Line Rating offers the potential to leverage the existing grid and improve integration of renewables while reducing grid congestion.

Climate change will impact wind and therefore wind power generation with largely unknown effect and magnitude; climate models can provide insights and should be used for long-term power planning, and location-aware predictions are important for wind power expansion.

The rise of distributed renewable generation creates computational challenges for operation and planning in networks with many buses and decentral generators; new linear optimal power flow formulations can solve multi-period LOPF with storage dispatch and generation capacity expansion significantly faster.

standard.summary: GraphARC is introduced as a benchmark for abstract reasoning on graph-structured data, motivated by the claim that relational reasoning lies at the heart of intelligence and that existing benchmarks are typically confined to formats such as grids or text. GraphARC generalizes the few-shot transformation learning paradigm of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) to graph-structured data, allowing tasks to scale across diverse graph families and sizes. Evaluation of state-of-the-art language models on GraphARC shows they can answer graph property questions but often fail at full graph transformation tasks, revealing a comprehension-execution gap and performance degradation on larger instances, which exposes scaling barriers and provides a testbed for future graph foundation models.

citations.claim: Relational reasoning lies at the heart of intelligence, but existing benchmarks are typically confined to formats such as grids or text.
We introduce GraphARC, a benchmark for abstract reasoning on graph-structured data.
GraphARC generalizes the few-shot transformation learning paradigm of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC).
Unlike grid-based ARC, GraphARC instances can be generated at scale across diverse graph families and sizes, enabling systematic evaluation of generalization abilities.
Models can answer questions about graph properties but often fail to solve the full graph transformation task, revealing a comprehension-execution gap.
Performance further degrades on larger instances, exposing scaling barriers.
By combining aspects of node classification, link prediction, and graph generation within a single framework, GraphARC provides a promising testbed for future graph foundation models.

Each task requires inferring a transformation rule from a few input-output pairs and applying it to a new test graph, covering local, global, and hierarchical graph transformations. GraphARC can be generated at scale across diverse graph families and sizes, enabling systematic evaluation of generalization. Evaluations of state-of-the-art language models reveal limitations: models can answer questions about graph properties but often fail at the full transformation task, and performance degrades on larger instances, exposing scaling barriers.
